newsitem.title: USA: N.J. pension bond vote may wait until June - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. pension bond vote may wait until June - paper.

text.p: A vote on New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman's proposal to sell $2.8 billion of pension bonds may not come until early June, the Star Ledger reported Tuesday.

Whitman had urged the legislature to move quickly to take advantage of the current low interest rate environment. But Senate President Donald DiFrancesco, R-Union, said the vote could be delayed until after the June 3 state primary. The earliest a vote would be possible is May 22, DiFrancesco said.
The Senate already cancelled one scheduled vote last month, after proponents of the bond sale could not muster enough support.

Whitman's plan envisions selling $2.8 billion of taxable bonds to eliminate the state's unfunded pension liability. The move would also free up nearly $600 million of budget savings by eliminating the need for the state's regular 1997 and 1998 pension system contributions.
